To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DOS and the resistivity of the graphene are strongly dependent on the location of the defects, while the thermal conductivity depends on both the location and the number of defects in the graphene.

the DOS, resistive and thermal conductivity of graphene at low temperature are determined by the structural defects of the short-range ordering type, which can be of two types, the location of defects and the location of defects with the formation of large-area cells.
the DOS, resistive and thermal conductivity of epitaxial graphene are determined by the presence of structural defects of short-range order.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the short-range structural order on the electronic properties of epitaxial graphene.
the influence of the short-range disorder and structural inhomogeneities on the electrical and thermal properties of graphene.
the study of the electronic properties of the graphene layer in the case of the presence of defects in its structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electronic structure of graphene is determined not only by the presence of defects, but also by the presence of the structural short-range order in graphene.

the presence of short-range order structures in epitaxial graphene leads to a significant change in its electronic and thermal properties, and therefore to the appearance of a new class of graphene-based materials.
the presence of the short-range structural order in graphene is a necessary condition for its metalization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of the structural inhomogeneous short-range order in the graphene layer is the main factor for the appearance of the gap in the DOS and the change in the temperature dependence of the relaxation time, resistivity and the thermal conductivity.
in order to obtain an effective description of the electronic properties of graphene it is necessary to take into account the short-range order of the structure.

in the presence of a large number of structural cells of short-range order in graphene, it is possible to obtain a significant decrease in the resistivity and thermal resistance of the layer, which will allow the use of graphene in the electronics and in the field of thermoelectrics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the temperature dependence of DOS, resistivity, thermal conductivity of graphene at low temperature can be explained by the presence of short-range order structures of the type of cells of large area.

a large number of defects and impurities in graphene are not necessarily a disadvantage, as the presence of such defects can be a factor in increasing the thermal conductivity and the mobility of the carriers.
a graphene layer with a short-range ordered structure can be used in the temperature region from 4 to 300 K as a material with a high conductivity and a high heat conductivity.
